title: Investigating the Thermal Degradation Mechanism of 2D Nb4C3Tx MXene through in-situ (S)TEM
content: MXenes have attracted increasing attention due to the unique low-dimensional structure and exceptional properties [1]. MXenes are novel 2-dimensional transition metal carbides prepared through etching the specific A layers of the MAX phase (the layered carbides and/or nitrides exhibit the general formula: Mn+1AXn (n = 1, 2 or 3), where M represents the early transition metals, A is a group A element, and X is C or N) [2-3]. MXenes show promising potential in wide range of energy storage applications such as lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), electrochemical supercapacitors and fuel cells [4-5]. However, one of the key obstacles for the practical application is the thermal stability of the MXene during the extreme working environment: the thermal degradation of the 2D structure itself as well as the complex heterostructures between the MXene layers can change the physical and chemical performances, thereby affecting the actual working state of the MXene-related electronic devices or electrochemical reactions. To date, only limited approaches have been proposed to investigate the thermal stability of the MXene structure. Therefore, it is of great importance to build in-depth understanding of thermal degradation process of 2D MXenes.
